name: Robertson Pie Shop
note: The highway pie that started a hundred optimistic detours. Grab one while it is still hot.

name: Fitzroy Falls
note: A lookout over the falls in Morton National Park, mist included on a good morning.

name: Bombo Headland Quarry
note: The old quarry headland at Kiama, where the rock is columnar and the sea is the colour of bottle glass.

name: Hyams Beach, Jervis Bay
note: A white-sand beach on Jervis Bay. The water really is that clear.

name: Murrays Beach, Booderee
note: A quiet beach in Booderee National Park, Jervis Bay Territory, facing Bowen Island. Park pass required.

name: Three Sisters, Blue Mountains
note: The three sandstone sisters, seen from Echo Point. The valley does the talking.

name: Sydney Opera House
note: The sails, from the forecourt. Go around sunset if the family can agree on a time.

name: Bondi to Coogee Coastal Walk
note: A clifftop walk that starts at Bondi Icebergs and ends at Coogee. Swim stops are the point.

name: Stockton Sand Dunes, Port Stephens
note: The huge dunes at Birubi Point, on Worimi country. Tours run out onto the sand from here.

name: Sea Cliff Bridge
note: The bridge that curves off the cliff at Clifton. Pull over before someone yells look.

name: South West Rocks and Trial Bay Gaol
note: A ruined seaside gaol at Trial Bay, above the beaches of South West Rocks.

name: Cape Byron Lighthouse
note: The lighthouse on the easternmost point of the Australian mainland. Whales pass in season.

name: Mount Kosciuszko
note: The summit of mainland Australia. The walk leaves from Thredbo, and the weather can turn.

name: Mungo National Park
note: The Walls of China on a dry lake in the Willandra Lakes. Stay on the boardwalk; this place is ancient and fragile.

name: Broken Hill
note: An outback mining city with the line of lode on the skyline. The desert starts at the end of the street.

name: Twelve Apostles
note: Limestone stacks in the Southern Ocean. The lookout is the view; the cliff edge is not a shortcut.

name: Loch Ard Gorge
note: The gorge of a famous shipwreck, a short walk from the Apostles. Check whether the beach steps are open.

name: Cape Otway Lightstation
note: A lightstation on the wild Otway coast, still watching Bass Strait.

name: The Pinnacle, Grampians (Gariwerd)
note: The rock balcony above Halls Gap. The Wonderland walk is the classic way up.

name: Sovereign Hill, Ballarat
note: A goldrush town that still runs. Candlelight tours if everyone can stay up.

name: Phillip Island Penguin Parade
note: Little penguins come ashore at dusk at Summerlands. Book it; the parade does not wait for late families.

name: Wilsons Promontory, Tidal River
note: Tidal River, the beach at the foot of Wilsons Prom. Wildlife has right of way.

name: Puffing Billy Railway
note: Steam trains from Belgrave into the Dandenong Ranges. Sit where the legs can dangle, if the carriage allows.

name: Brighton Bathing Boxes
note: A row of bright bathing boxes on Dendy Street Beach. They are photographs, not cubbyhouses.

name: Queen Victoria Market
note: Melbourne's market halls. Go hungry, leave with more than you planned.

name: Healesville Sanctuary
note: A bush sanctuary in the Yarra Valley. The platypus dusk tour is the quiet show.

name: Mount Buffalo
note: The old chalet and the gorge lookouts on a hanging plateau above the Ovens Valley.

name: Beechworth Historic Precinct
note: A gold-town street of granite buildings, Ned Kelly stories included.

name: Silo Art Trail, Brim
note: The painted silos at Brim, first of the Silo Art Trail. Blink and the highway has gone past them.

name: Great Barrier Reef, Agincourt Reef
note: A ribbon reef out from Port Douglas. You only get there by a permitted boat; the pontoon is the visit, not a beach car park.

name: Mossman Gorge
note: A rainforest river on Kuku Yalanji country, with a walk beside the boulders.

name: Cape Tribulation
note: Where the rainforest meets the reef. The beach is the destination, and cassowaries have right of way.

name: Whitehaven Beach
note: The long white beach on Whitsunday Island. It is a boat day, not a driveway.

name: Lake McKenzie (Boorangoora), K'gari
note: A perched lake of white sand on K'gari. Swim, then leave the sand on the beach, not in your towel.

name: Noosa National Park
note: The coastal track at Noosa Heads. Boiling Pot lookout is the postcard stop.

name: Australia Zoo
note: The big zoo at Beerwah. Crocodiles at feeding time, shade at lunch.

name: Springbrook National Park, Natural Bridge
note: A waterfall that falls through a rock arch. Glow-worms show up after dark if you stay quiet.

name: Lamington National Park, O'Reilly's
note: The rainforest balcony at O'Reilly's in Lamington. Birds will try to join breakfast.

name: Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary
note: A creek-side wildlife park at Currumbin. The lorikeets have opinions.

name: Magnetic Island Forts Walk
note: World War II forts on Magnetic Island, with a view back across the water to Townsville.

name: Paronella Park
note: A Spanish-style castle in the rainforest, built for a sweetheart. The hydro still runs.

name: Undara Lava Tubes
note: Lava tubes you see with a guide and a lamp. The savannah around Undara does the driving.

name: Australian Age of Dinosaurs, Winton
note: A working dinosaur museum on a jump-up outside Winton. Fossils, not a theme park.

name: Cape York, The Tip (Pajinka)
note: The northern tip of the continent, Pajinka, on Gudang and Yadhaykenu country. Remote, permit country, and a long way from a servo.

name: Wilpena Pound (Ikara)
note: The natural amphitheatre of Ikara. This pin is the visitor hub at Wilpena, where the walks begin.

name: Brachina Gorge
note: A drive through deep time in the Flinders Ranges. The Golden Spike marks the start of the Ediacaran.

name: Coober Pedy
note: An opal town that lives underground. A dugout is cooler than the street at noon.

name: Farina Historic Township
note: A ghost town on the old Ghan route, looked after by volunteers. The bakery opens in season.

name: Remarkable Rocks, Kangaroo Island
note: Granite boulders on a dome above the Southern Ocean, in Flinders Chase.

name: Seal Bay, Kangaroo Island
note: A boardwalk through a sea-lion colony. Stay on it; they are not posing.

name: Kuitpo Forest
note: Stringybark forest in the Adelaide Hills. Picnic tables below, koalas if you look up.

name: Victor Harbor and Granite Island
note: The causeway from Victor Harbor lands on Granite Island. Little penguins, big wind.

name: Naracoorte Caves
note: Fossil caves at Naracoorte, a World Heritage ground-sloth kind of place.

name: Umpherston Sinkhole (Balumbul)
note: A sinkhole garden in Mount Gambier, also called Balumbul. Stairs down into the ferns.

name: Coffin Bay National Park
note: Point Avoid lookout, the sealed-road view over the cliffs and Avoid Bay.

name: Adelaide Central Market
note: Adelaide's covered market. The jam donut is not a rumour.

name: The Pinnacles, Nambung
note: Thousands of limestone pillars in the yellow sand of Nambung National Park. Dawn is the quiet version.

name: Rottnest Island (Wadjemup)
note: Thomson Bay settlement on Wadjemup. Bikes, quokkas, and a ferry from Fremantle.

name: Turquoise Bay, Ningaloo
note: A beach in Cape Range where Ningaloo Reef starts under your feet. Read the current signs before you drift.

name: Monkey Mia
note: Dolphins that still visit the shallows. The ranger talk is part of the visit.

name: Kalbarri Skywalk
note: Two platforms out over the Murchison gorge. The path is flat; the drop is not.

name: Wave Rock (Hyden Rock)
note: A granite wave north of Hyden. It is exactly as advertised, which is rare.

name: Lucky Bay, Cape Le Grand
note: A bay in Cape Le Grand where kangaroos use the beach. The sand is seriously white.

name: Valley of the Giants Tree Top Walk
note: A steel walk through the red tingle canopy near Walpole. The Ancient Empire boardwalk is the ground-level version.

name: Busselton Jetty
note: The long jetty at Busselton. Walk it, or let the little train do the middle.

name: Jewel Cave, Augusta
note: A show cave in the Leeuwin-Naturaliste ridge, near Augusta. Stalactites, and a guided descent.

name: Karijini National Park, Dales Gorge
note: Fern pools and Fortescue Falls in Dales Gorge. The trail has stairs, and a swim at the bottom.

name: Cable Beach, Broome
note: The wide sunset beach at Broome. Camels are optional. The tides are not small.

name: Horizontal Falls (Garaanngaddim)
note: A tidal waterfall in Talbot Bay. You see it from a boat or a plane, with permission on Dambimangari country. There is no road to the falls.

name: Bungle Bungle Range, Purnululu
note: The beehive domes. Cathedral Gorge leaves from Piccaninny car park. The road in is seasonal and 4WD only.

name: Cradle Mountain, Dove Lake
note: The boatshed view of Cradle Mountain across Dove Lake. The circuit is the family classic.

name: Wineglass Bay Lookout
note: The lookout over the curved bay in Freycinet. The beach is a longer walk down.

name: Bay of Fires, Binalong Bay
note: Orange lichen rocks at Binalong Bay, the easy end of the Bay of Fires.

name: Port Arthur Historic Site
note: The convict ruins on the Tasman Peninsula. The harbour is beautiful and the history is not soft.

name: Salamanca Market
note: Saturday stalls in the sandstone warehouses at Salamanca Place. Go before the fudge stalls win.

name: kunanyi / Mount Wellington
note: The summit of kunanyi. The lookout is often in the cloud, which is its own view.

name: Bruny Island, The Neck
note: The isthmus lookout on Bruny. Penguins on one side, surf on the other.

name: Maria Island, Darlington and Painted Cliffs
note: The ferry lands at Darlington. Wombats treat the lawns as theirs, and the Painted Cliffs are a low-tide walk.

name: Tasman Arch
note: A rock arch in the sea cliffs, with the Devil's Kitchen next door.

name: Cataract Gorge, Launceston
note: A gorge in the middle of Launceston, with a pool, peacocks, and a chairlift if the legs vote no.

name: Stanley, The Nut
note: The volcanic plug above Stanley. The chairlift is the kind option; the path is the smug one.

name: Russell Falls, Mount Field
note: A short walk to a waterfall in Mount Field, ferns the whole way.

name: Uluru Base Walk
note: The walk around the base of Uluru. The climb is closed. Start early and carry more water than you think.

name: Kata Tjuta, Valley of the Winds
note: A walk in among the domes. The full circuit is a real hike; Karu Lookout is the shorter turn. This pin is the car park.

name: Kings Canyon, Watarrka
note: The rim walk at Watarrka. Canyon walls, a garden at the bottom, and a long stair.

name: Ormiston Gorge
note: A waterhole in the West MacDonnells, with ghost gums and a gorge walk.

name: Standley Chasm (Angkerle Atwatye)
note: A narrow cleft in the range, on private Aboriginal land. Midday is when the light drops in.

name: Alice Springs Desert Park
note: Desert habitats in one walkable park on the edge of Alice Springs, nocturnal house included.

name: Devils Marbles (Karlu Karlu)
note: The rounded boulders of Karlu Karlu. Walk the loop and leave every rock where it is.

name: Nitmiluk Gorge
note: The gorge at Nitmiluk, on Jawoyn country. A boat, or a walk above the first gorge.

name: Litchfield National Park, Florence Falls
note: A plunge pool at Florence Falls. The stairs down are the price of the swim.

name: Ubirr, Kakadu
note: Rock art and a floodplain lookout at Ubirr. Sunset is the famous version. The art sites close for part of the day.

name: Yellow Water (Ngurrungurrudjba), Kakadu
note: The wetland at Ngurrungurrudjba, near Cooinda. Cruises are how you visit. Crocodiles live here; they are not the entertainment.

name: Mindil Beach, Darwin
note: Darwin's sunset beach. The markets take over in the dry season.

name: Questacon
note: The national science centre. The buttons are meant to be pressed.

name: Australian War Memorial
note: The memorial at the end of Anzac Parade. Give it more time than you think.

name: National Arboretum Canberra
note: A hundred forests on a Canberra ridge, with a view back to the lake.

name: Tidbinbilla Nature Reserve
note: A valley sanctuary on the edge of Namadgi. Start at the visitor centre and pick a short walk.

name: Mount Ainslie Lookout
note: The lookout over Canberra from the hill behind the War Memorial. A short uphill from the car park.

name: Australian National Botanic Gardens
note: The national gardens on the slopes of Black Mountain. Walk the rainforest gully.
